items.title: What if you didn’t brush your teeth for a year? - Justin Merritt
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Trace the impact that not brushing or flossing can have on your teeth, gums, microbiome, and overall health over time.

--

At any given time, your mouth is maintaining a delicate balance between hundreds of microbial species, which is why dentists agree that you should brush twice and floss once every day. But what if you just… didn’t? If you stopped doing any oral hygiene, how long would it take for your mouth to get messy? Justin Merritt investigates how not brushing can impact your health over time.

Lesson by Justin Merritt, directed by Lee Oz, Eliška Oz, Oz Animation.

items.title: Scary stories to watch in the dark (if you dare…)
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>This Halloween, dig into a collection of 6 chilling tales of blood-thirsty creatures, a cursed talisman, vengeful ghosts, and more.

--

At TED-Ed we pride ourselves on sparking curiosity and facilitating learning, but we all know that some lessons are only learned the hard way, and that curiosity killed any number of fools. Take a moment to learn from the greedy, the cruel, and the foolhardy with a collection of six of our favorite terrifying tales. Watch it after dark... if you dare.

items.title: 5 sneaky ways stores get you to spend more
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore 5 tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how to avoid being tricked.

--

You’re about to buy some bargain bin headphones when you spot another sale. A different pair that is more expensive, but selling for half their usual price. Which is the better buy? And how do you know you’re not falling for a retailer’s psychological tricks? Explore common tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how you can avoid being tricked.

Directed by Homework Studio.

items.title: Why does this animal never age? - Raymond Adkins
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the incredible regenerative abilities of hydras, and get to know their biology to find out if they're really immortal. 

--

In 1740, naturalist Abraham Trembley found something shocking in pondwater. He couldn't tell if it was a plant or an animal, though its way of moving and consuming things seemed animal-like. But when he cut parts off or even split it in two, it regenerated, which was decidedly plant-like. So, what was this miraculous creature? Raymond Adkins explores the near-immortal biology of the hydra.

Lesson by Raymond Adkins, directed by Sharon Colman.

items.title: 3 things to never do with a credit card
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Learn how to spot the 3 most common traps of credit cards, and how they can lock you into a cycle of interest, fees, and debt.

--

While useful for secure purchasing, emergencies, and building credit scores, credit cards can make it difficult to avoid overspending. And this is no accident. Credit card systems are intentionally designed to encourage spending and lock you into a cycle of interest and fees. So, how can you avoid their most common traps? Explore 3 ways that credit card companies take advantage of their customers.

Directed by Jeff Le Bars, JetPropulsion.space.

items.title: How to present your ideas effectively
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Episode 10: Dig into 3 ways you can reveal ideas to your audience, and how each of these strategies can be employed most effectively.

--

This is episode 10 of the animated series, “Public Speaking 101.” Ideas change everything — and since language lets us share our ideas, learning how to use it well gives speakers the power to inspire people and even change how they think. This 11-episode course will teach you how to identify, develop, and share your best ideas, while mastering essential communication skills along the way.

Directed by Tolga Yıldız, Kozmonot Animation Studio.

The TED-Ed Student Talks program provides free, customizable activities for educators to support their students in identifying, developing and sharing their ideas with each other and the world. Learn more at https://ed.ted.com/student_talks

items.title: Which is better: Buying or renting a home? - Ella Feldman
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Dig into the dilemma of whether it's financially better to rent or buy a home, and explore the pros and cons of each choice.

--

Nobody was surprised when Morgan and her twin sister Lisa moved into identical houses right next to each other. The only difference? Morgan bought her house, while Lisa is renting hers. For generations, conventional wisdom has been that homeownership is financially better than renting. But is this actually true? Ella Feldman follows the twins in their housing journey to see who comes out on top.

Lesson by Ella Feldman, directed by Josh Pilch, Augenblick Studios.

items.title: Why is Queen Victoria so controversial? - Carolyn Harris
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Queen Victoria presided over a golden age of the British Empire — but was she its moral compass or obsessed with her reputation?

--

During her 63-year reign, Queen Victoria was a model of morality and restraint. So much so that the 19th century is called the “Victorian Age” and is still associated with these qualities. But was she the empire’s moral compass during a time of dizzying change, or an imperialist monarch who cared more about her reputation than her subjects? Carolyn Harris puts this controversial figure on trial.

Lesson by Carolyn Harris, directed by Igor Ćorić, Artrake Studio.
